correctness.rationale: At state \(j\), the test level is \(a_j=\alpha q\gamma_j\). Because \(a_j\le\lambda\), rejection \(P\le a_j\) and state advancement \(\lambda<P\le\tau\) are disjoint and have probabilities \(a_j\) and \(q\); all other outcomes leave the state unchanged. Conditioning on the almost-sure first occurrence of either terminating event gives rejection probability \(\alpha\gamma_j/(1+\alpha\gamma_j)\) and survival probability \((1+\alpha\gamma_j)^{-1}\). Multiplying survival through the states and using continuity from above proves the infinite product. The lower envelope follows by expanding \(\prod_j(1+\alpha\gamma_j)\ge1+\alpha\), with equality only for one-point spending; the strict upper envelope follows from \(\sum_j\log(1+\alpha\gamma_j)<\alpha\), and uniform-on-\(N\) spending approaches the supremum. Euler's product for \(\sinh\) gives the inverse-square specialization. The inspected checker only corroborates finite recursions and numerical identities; the infinite result is proved analytically.

value.rationale: The result quantifies a known and practically relevant conservatism of a named online FWER method exactly, separates the effect of the spending sequence from the discard thresholds in the complete-null regime, and identifies the sharp possible range together with a closed form for a published inverse-square schedule. This is a natural statistical invariant of the procedure rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
residual_risks: The law is deliberately confined to the exact-uniform complete null and therefore does not measure power or strong-FWER behavior under alternatives.

final_claim: For ADDIS-Spending with fixed \(0<\lambda<\tau\le1\), \(q=\tau-\lambda\), nonnegative \((\gamma_j)\) summing to one, independent exact-uniform complete-null p-values, and \(\alpha q\gamma_j\le\lambda\), the infinite-stream FWER is exactly \(1-\prod_{j\ge1}(1+\alpha\gamma_j)^{-1}\). Over all spending sequences it ranges from the attained minimum \(\alpha/(1+\alpha)\) to the unattained supremum \(1-e^{-\alpha}\); for \(\gamma_j=6/(\pi^2j^2)\) it equals \(1-\sqrt{6\alpha}/\sinh(\sqrt{6\alpha})\).
limitations: The equality uses independent exact-uniform complete-null p-values and fixed thresholds.
The containment condition \(\alpha(\tau-\lambda)\gamma_j\le\lambda\) is essential to the two-competing-events state reduction.
No formula is claimed for dependent or merely conservative nulls, false-null mixtures, ADDIS-Graph, or exhaustive ADDIS.
